correctness.rationale: The exact LCF graph gives eighteen edges. Two distinct standalone programs enumerate 1025 nonempty matchings with face vector (18,117,333,397,152,8). A fixed edge-label Morse pivot order produces exactly 502 pairs and critical cells (1 in dimension 0, 20 in dimension 3) for the full complex. For each of all eighteen edge deletions the same construction leaves exactly one 0-cell and the claimed number of 3-cells; the included complete pair and critical-face certificate is checked against all faces. Every directed codimension-one incidence is reconstructed and exhaustively topologically sorted, proving acyclicity. Forman discrete Morse gives a CW complex with only a vertex and 3-cells and therefore the claimed integral wedge of S^3. Independent GF(2) boundary ranks (17,100,233,144,8) and all deletion ranks corroborate. The proof is finite and exhaustive only for the 19 stated complexes, not a numerical extrapolation.

evidence: The Frucht graph is a cubic three-connected planar Halin graph with trivial automorphism group, not a tree, simple cycle, or outerplanar graph.
Engström (arxiv:math/0512420) gives connectivity estimates for claw-free independence complexes, not exact Frucht matching-complex homotopy and all eighteen deletions.
Wachs 2003 surveys bounded-degree graph-complex methods; Jonsson 2008 has a matching-complex chapter concentrating on complete graphs, chessboards, paths and cycles (accessible table of contents).

Bayer et al. (2020) classifies graph matching complexes that are homology manifolds; a wedge of twenty 3-spheres is not a homology manifold. The outerplanar results address a graph class excluding this cubic three-connected example.

value.rationale: The Frucht graph is a canonical minimal cubic asymmetric graph. Its edge matching complex is a standard natural topological invariant, but the full homotopy type and sensitivity under every edge deletion are not implied by a matching polynomial or by symmetry. Determining all eighteen cases matters especially because no nontrivial automorphism relates the edges; the seven distinct three-sphere ranks provide a complete local topological fingerprint and make a substantive comparison to previously studied symmetric cubic graphs. The exact integral homotopy classification and uniform acyclic Morse certificate provide information beyond face counts or a small negative check.
